label: sparse g-history-related reset feature (unexplained)
explanation: Very sparse (0.036% of steps, never at t<3, not on incorrect-copy steps). Enriched for sequences containing g (in_tok g 10.6x lift, out_tok g 15.6x, first_tok g 10x) and secondarily b/t/y, and for recall_idx 2 / short L=3-4 sequences, but no tested predicate reached precision above ~7%: input g, g in the first two originals, multiple g seen, g plus t/y/digit in the prefix, and copy-phase in_tok==out_tok==g (best F1 0.08) all have very low precision. Many activations sit on non-g tokens (b, j, p, <DEL>) in sequences that contain g earlier, so firing seems to depend on a specific hidden-state configuration not captured by token-level variables. Magnitude is narrow (median 0.12, max 0.24), with the strongest activations in copy-phase steps inputting g in short g-containing sequences.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=g (+5.29), phase=2 & in_tok=b (+5.00), out_tok=g (+3.75), orig0=g (+3.17), out_tok=y (+2.90), prev_tok=h (+2.63). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-4.37), prev_tok=w (-3.20), prev_tok=t (-2.78), orig_idx=-1 (-2.74).
